note: Asking prices in euros from the original listing on the day each home was added. Medians describe the homes RealHunt lists (cheap for their country, checked by a person), not a country's whole market. Rules, taxes and costs are general information, not legal or tax advice.
sentences: On 28 November 2026, RealHunt lists 3 homes for sale in Slovenia, each one checked by a person.
In Slovenia, the median asking price of those 3 homes is €140,000 (€1,123 per m², from the 3 homes with a known size); the cheapest costs €105,000 and the most expensive €229,000.
With 3 homes this is a small sample, so the median for Slovenia is a rough guide.

buying.costs_breakdown: Real estate transfer tax (davek na promet nepremičnin) of 2%, paid by the seller unless the sales contract says the buyer pays it.
buying.can_foreigners_buy: Yes for citizens of EU, EEA and OECD countries (such as the United States, the United Kingdom and Canada), who buy like Slovenians. Citizens of EU candidate countries (North Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine, Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Georgia) first need a decision confirming reciprocity, and citizens of other countries, such as China and Russia, cannot buy, only inherit where reciprocity exists.
buying.annual_property_tax: The direct user of the home, usually the owner, pays a yearly fee for the use of building land (nadomestilo za uporabo stavbnega zemljišča, NUSZ), set by each municipality's ordinance and assessed once a year by the tax administration (FURS); owners of holiday homes also pay property tax (davek od premoženja).

homes.title: Well maintained detached house with garden and fireplace in Spodnji Ivanjci, Pomurje
homes.title_es: Casa independiente bien mantenida con jardín y chimenea en Spodnji Ivanjci, Pomurje
homes.summary: This well maintained detached house, built in 1989, stands on a 1,015 m² plot in a quiet hilly setting. It offers 2 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, a living room opening onto a glazed winter garden, and a basement cellar. Extras include a garden, a balcony, a wood-burning fireplace, a garage with carport and a cellar. It is heated by central radiators with a pellet boiler and lies about 12 km from Gornja Radgona and 8 km from the Pomurje motorway. Asking €140,000, about €787/m².

homes.title: Renovated two-flat house with a vineyard and vaulted wine cellar near Gornja Radgona
homes.title_es: Casa de dos pisos renovada con viña y bodega abovedada cerca de Gornja Radgona
homes.summary: A house of 204 m² on 6,117 m² of land, a five-minute drive from the centre of Gornja Radgona, split into two separate four-room flats with their own entrances, each with a kitchen, living room, three bedrooms and a bathroom. It has been renovated over the years with new wiring and plumbing, quality windows, a new tiled roof, an insulated facade, a heat pump, heat recovery ventilation, air conditioning and fibre internet; energy class B1. Below is a vaulted wine cellar with climate control, and outside a 73.5 m² outbuilding with a garage, an orchard, raised beds and about 200 white vines. Sold fully furnished, with building and use permits.

homes.title: Restored Prekmurje farmhouse with antique furniture in Ivanjševci, Goričko
homes.title_es: Casa de labranza de Prekmurje restaurada con muebles antiguos en Ivanjševci, Goričko
homes.summary: A traditional Prekmurje house from about 1900 in the quiet village of Ivanjševci in the Goričko hills, close to the Hungarian border, carefully adapted in 2010 to 2012. The roof, floors and plaster are new, with new double windows made in the old style, made-to-measure doors and a fresh facade. About 78 m²: an entrance porch, a shower room with WC, a living room, a fitted kitchen with dining area and a bedroom, heated by wood stoves. A 75 m² old farm building and a field come with it, 1,814 m² in all. Both buildings have permits and the title is clear. Energy class F.
